page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.medium is an entry-level general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It provides 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) running at 2.8 GHz with a non-hyperthreaded single-thread-per-core layout. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory is sized at 4.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM profile. In addition to a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, the instance includes 59 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. There are no discrete GPU accelerators available.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance alongside the natural scaling constraints of a single-core environment. The instance achieves a single-core score of 1,735.0 in Geekbench and 1,693.28 in stress-ng single-core execution. Compression and decompression tasks show capable execution rates, registering 30.03 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.02 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Conversely, parallel execution is constrained by the 1-vCPU count, resulting in lower scores on multi-core metrics such as Geekbench multi-core (1,738.0) and stress-ng multi-core (1,693.28). Memory throughput tests record 30.15 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads, while static web serving throughput reaches 2.33 GB/sec and Redis SET performance delivers 2.35 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure cost-efficiency perspective, m8gd.medium provides predictable single-core performance without the CPU contention or throttling associated with burstable instances. The integration of high-speed local NVMe storage reduces external EBS dependencies for workloads that rely heavily on temporary scratch disk space or local caching. This hardware profile aligns well with lightweight web serving, microservices, continuous integration runners, background task workers, and staging environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.medium is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System using an ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Configured with 1 dedicated vCPU operating at 2.8 GHz and 4.0 GB of system memory, it preserves a standard 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio. The hardware package bundles 59 GB of fast local NVMe SSD instance storage and offers 1 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPU hardware. Single-core processing demonstrates steady performance, delivering 14.02 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,735.0, though parallel workload capacity remains limited to its single physical core. Combining dedicated processor allocation with bundled high-speed ephemeral NVMe storage, the m8gd.medium is well suited for lightweight microservices, background job processing, small caching layers, and development testing environments requiring predictable single-thread execution.
